text:
Registered residential sales totaled 10,195 units worth AED 27,672,330,524 in the last four weeks, a 6.1% decline in volume and 1.3% drop in value compared to the previous period. Mortgage registrations stood at 4,054, recorded separately from sales. The off-plan share of transactions decreased to 59.4% from 66.6% in the prior four weeks, indicating a shift in transaction mix.

The median residential price per square foot fell to AED 1,666, down 1.8% from AED 1,697. Top performing areas by sales volume over twelve weeks include Dubai South with 3,850 units and Jumeirah Village Circle with 2,310 units. Dubai South maintained a median price of AED 1,692.8 per square foot with a 0.6% decline, while Jumeirah Village Circle saw a 2.5% price drop to AED 1,409.25 per square foot.

Rental activity remained robust with 92,516 Ejari contracts registered, where 50.2% were renewals. The median residential rent held steady at AED 70,000 annually. Estimated gross yields for flats show Zaabeel First leading at 9.1%, followed by International City Phase 1 at 8.6% and Town Square at 6.9%. These figures reflect the ratio of median annual rent to median price per square foot for specific property types.

The watch list highlights Al Yufrah 1 with a 36.8% price increase over twelve weeks, contrasting with Liwan which cooled by 14.6%. Palm Deira and Palm Jumeirah both recorded 13.2% and 13.3% declines respectively. An anomaly monitor flagged 1,067 sales in the last 60 days priced more than 35% away from comparable medians. Figures are derived from registered DLD data and Ejari contracts using medians and benchmark filters that exclude bulk deals and outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
